discoveries.title: How these markets actually settle
discoveries.body: Measured before launch on 200 resolved markets: comparing Chainlink's 60-second TWAP at the close with the 60-second TWAP at the open reproduced Polymarket's official result 99% of the time (using Binance as a stand-in), while the open/close numbers from Polymarket's crypto-price endpoint matched only 88.5%. So the AI computes the price to beat itself and settles trades only on the official resolution.

discoveries.title: Settlement rule check
discoveries.body: The AI's own rule (60-second Chainlink TWAP at the close vs at the open) matched Polymarket's official result in 925 of 981 markets (94.3%). Mismatches happened only when the margin was tiny (median 2.55 bp).

discoveries.title: The market beats the fair-value model
discoveries.body: Over 60 markets the market price was more accurate than S002's model (its log loss was 0.052 worse per market, and still worse at the edge of the 95% confidence range). Trading against a more accurate market loses money, so real paper trades stop. All strategies keep trading virtually; the first one to show a statistically significant profit takes over.

discoveries.title: No tradable pattern yet
discoveries.body: Tested 65 signal/time combinations on 1154 markets. None beats the market price by enough to cover fees yet. Closest: 3-minute momentum at 150s (+2.1 points vs the price, n=664). The AI keeps collecting data.

discoveries.title: UP/DOWN base rate
discoveries.body: UP won 48.0% of the last 1151 markets - consistent with 50/50 (±2.9%).

discoveries.title: Model accuracy vs the market
discoveries.body: The market price is more accurate than the champion model (0.0017 Brier gap over 1066 markets). Edges are hard to find; the AI should stay selective.

discoveries.title: What moves these markets
discoveries.body: Signals that point the right way most often (measured on 1154 markets): 3-minute momentum at 150s right 82% of the time (n=664, the market price itself was right 83%); 3-minute momentum at 90s right 73% of the time (n=805, the market price itself was right 76%); 1-minute momentum at 30s right 70% of the time (n=852, the market price itself was right 71%). Pointing the right way is not enough to profit: it also has to beat the price you pay.
